*Kusalattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 16.1) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka in the Pali Canon [Catalog]. Structurally, the text treats the analytical intersection of the triad on wholesome, unwholesome, and undetermined phenomena (*kusalattika*) with the dyad of root conditions (*hetuduka*), analyzing the conditional relations operating across these categories [Catalog].

 However, computational analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates widespread formulaic text reuse within the Pali Abhidhamma, registering 806 matching passages across 103 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The strongest internal reuse links occur with closely related sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, most notably *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1), *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1), *Kusalattika, Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 4.2), and parallel matrix formulations in Patthana 10.1 and 22.1, in addition to the non-canonical *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā Abhidhammapiṭaka* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with Sanskrit and Tibetan technical treatises, including the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, Chapter 1 of the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya*, and its Tibetan translation/commentary (*Abhidharmakośaṭīkā-lakṣaṇānusāriṇī*), reflecting shared technical Abhidharma terminology on root conditions and psychological phenomena [DharmaNexus].
